facts.statement: The specimen was displayed at the Golden Gate International Exposition and the University of California Berkeley before being stored in the 1960s.
facts.quote: After being excavated, UCMP 33912 was mounted for display, first at the Golden Gate International Exposition, then at the University of California Berkeley, where it remained until being put into storage in the 1960s.

facts.statement: In 1943, Samuel Paul Welles identified the specimen as distinct enough to describe as a new genus and species, naming it Hydrotherosaurus alexandrae.
facts.quote: In 1943, American paleontologist Samuel Paul Welles found that the specimen was notably different from other known plesiosaurs and declared it as the type specimen of a new genus and species which he named Hydrotherosaurus alexandrae.

facts.statement: Hydrotherosaurus was a medium-sized plesiosaur estimated to be 7.8 to 8.8 meters long and weigh around 1.9 metric tons.
facts.quote: Hydrotherosaurus was a medium-sized plesiosaur, with an estimated body length of 7.8 - 8.8 m long and body mass of around 1.9 MT.

facts.statement: It possesses one of the longest necks relative to body length among elasmosaurids, containing 60 vertebrae in total.
facts.quote: It has one of the longest necks relative to total length among elasmosaurids, with 60 vertebrae in total.

facts.statement: The animal lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.

facts.statement: Hydrotherosaurus measured approximately 7.8 meters in length.
facts.quote: Hydrotherosaurus midió aproximadamente 7.8 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: It had a small head about 33 cm long, an aerodynamic body, and four large flippers specially designed to help the animal balance, move, and accelerate.
facts.quote: Tenía una cabeza pequeña que medía unos 33 centímetros de largo, un cuerpo aerodinámico y cuatro aletas grandes que fueron especialmente diseñadas para ayudar al enorme animal a equilibrarse, moverse y acelerarse.
